plates.title: Current TSH2 system architecture
plates.subtitle: One finite file, one numerical epoch, two separately returned output streams.
review_notes: The two HPS activities are one serialized service, not two processors or two FPGA cores.
No live codec input, UDP transport, online software-DSP replacement or board programming belongs in this plate.
review_callouts: 50 MHz fabric; unpaced finite-file input at nominal 48 kHz sample interpretation.
HPS RAM buffers are ordinary CPU memory. The FPGA-to-DDR ring writer is not active.
TSP1 has powers without phase. Audio reconstruction comes from the separate Y path.

notes.title: Finite, unpaced correctness path
notes.body: One file and full tail per START. 48 kHz is the sample interpretation, not a real-time throughput claim.

notes.title: Active boundary
notes.body: Ordinary HPS RAM buffers; no active FPGA DDR ring, UDP or live codec. TSP1 cannot reconstruct audio without the separate Y path.

plates.title: DSP datapath and finite-frame ownership
plates.subtitle: The same 256 / 128 geometry drives arithmetic, threshold ownership and the exact full tail.
review_notes: Full finite geometry: frames=floor((Ns+254)/128), tau_last=128*frames, Ny=tau_last+384.
The packet path receives pre-mask power plus the mask decision; sparse output omits masked bins, dense output writes zero for them.
Core metric logic exists, but the current TSH2 hardware protocol does not export the broader original per-frame METRICS/WAVE telemetry records.
Delayed-reference history participates in input ready/acceptance; this is not a valid-only observation tap.
review_callouts: Ns=384,000; frames=3,001; analysis tokens=384,128; full Y=384,512.
Frame 0 covers conceptual sample indices -128 through 127; its left half is zero.
THR2 equality is retained. Nyquist is eligible. The frame snapshot prevents mixed thresholds.

notes.title: Threshold ownership
notes.body: DC is protected; Nyquist is eligible; equality is retained. First frame covers indices -128..127 with a zero left half.

plates.title: FFT / IFFT engines and storage
plates.subtitle: Two separate iterative engines reuse a radix-2 butterfly and explicitly scheduled synchronous work RAM.
review_notes: This diagram is a template instantiated independently by FFT and IFFT; it is not one RAM shared by both engines.
The registered butterfly has five arithmetic register stages and a held result. Engine source describes seven-clock butterfly transactions; this is not a whole-frame or network latency claim.
RAM contents/read registers are not asynchronously cleared. All locations are loaded before compute; read and write schedules do not overlap, and the two butterfly addresses differ.
Use no arithmetic throughput or 48 kHz real-time acceptance claim derived solely from this structural schedule.
review_callouts: Eight radix-2 stages x 128 butterflies = 1,024 butterflies per transform.
Forward FFT divides by 2 at every stage; inverse FFT does not. Do not reverse these scaling labels.
Round-to-nearest, ties away from zero, followed by signed saturation.

notes.title: Separate FFT and IFFT instances
notes.body: Each engine owns its own RAM and butterfly. Eight stages x 128 butterflies = 1,024 butterflies per transform.

notes.title: Scaling and storage discipline
notes.body: FFT divides by 2 per stage; IFFT does not. Ties round away from zero, then saturate. Work RAM is reloaded, not asynchronously cleared.

plates.title: Finite epoch, sample ownership and completion
plates.subtitle: Host pauses preserve overlap/history; a completed core can still leave output bytes for the host to drain.
review_notes: The real PCM, analysis flush and WOLA drain phases are logical token domains, not wall-clock intervals.
For input lengths other than 384000 in admitted simulations, calculate the geometry rather than assuming 128 analysis zeros.
The HPS controller interleaves reads/writes throughout RUN and continues draining after DONE. It never waits to upload all PCM into the 256-entry fabric FIFO first.
review_callouts: One START owns the entire file and full tail. Chunk boundaries do not create reset or new epochs.
DONE means production complete, not that the host or laptop has received every byte.
CLEAR drops ownership and sticky faults but preserves the epoch counter; hardware reset resets epoch.

notes.title: Feed and drain throughout RUN
notes.body: The HPS interleaves PCM writes with Y and spectral reads. Chunk boundaries do not reset the core or start new epochs.

notes.title: Production completion is not host reception
notes.body: DONE can leave FIFO data unread. The host continues draining and verifies output totals before explicit CLEAR.

notes.title: Ownership reset versus hardware reset
notes.body: CLEAR preserves the epoch counter; hardware reset resets it. These are logical token phases, not measured wall-clock intervals.

plates.title: Two output paths: reconstructed Y and spectral TSP1
plates.subtitle: Waveform samples and spectral powers have different semantics, buffering and byte counts.
review_notes: Header offsets: magic0, version4, encoding6, config8, payload length12, frame16, threshold24, entry count32, flags34, reserved36, checksum40; payload begins48.
Checksum covers header bytes0..39 and payload/padding, excluding the stored checksum itself. It is FNV-1a64, not CRC.
Sparse K=129 at threshold zero yields1080bytes/frame, larger than dense952. Do not imply sparse always saves bytes.
Packet bytes count only the spectral representation. Y has384512*4=1538048 bytes in the full run, separately returned. TSP1 has no phase and cannot reconstruct the waveform by itself.
No legacy32-byte telemetry header, SPEC129 compression shift, METRICS, STATUS UDP record or DDR64-byte alignment belongs here.
review_callouts: Sparse: 48 + 8K bytes/frame. Each entry is bin index8 + power56; DC is always present, so 1 <= K <= 129.
Dense: 129 x 7 power bytes + header + 1 zero pad byte = 952 bytes/frame.
Finite TCP service selects sparse. The lower-level adapter and tests also support dense.

notes.title: Power packets are separate from waveform samples
notes.body: TSP1 stores squared magnitudes without phase. Full Y is 384,512 x 4 = 1,538,048 bytes and remains a separate output. The TCP service selects sparse; the adapter also supports dense.

notes.title: Sparse record: 48 + 8K bytes
notes.body: Each entry is bin8 + power56. DC is retained, so 1 <= K <= 129. At K=129, sparse is 1,080 bytes per frame.

notes.title: Dense record: 952 bytes
notes.body: 48-byte header + 129 x 7-byte powers + one pad byte. Sparse does not always save bytes. Byte counts do not describe WAV compression.

plates.title: Laptop TCP, HPS software and MMIO transport
plates.subtitle: Complete input reception precedes accelerator execution; the response carries both full outputs.
review_notes: Request magic0x31515254; header< I Q I >: magic, threshold, input byte count. Reply magic0x31535254; header< I I I I Q Q Q >: magic,status,Y bytes,TSP1 bytes,epoch,board wall ns,board thread CPU ns.
Socket upload/reply and idle accept have10s deadlines; controller has45s epoch deadline; process alarm60s. A blocked MMIO bus cannot be interrupted by its own polling deadline.
Failed requests terminate the service without automatic retry/MMIO recovery. Exact reference gold is not uploaded to the FPGA.
Do not draw FPGA-to-HPS DMA, a reserved DDR ring or UDP. HPS uses physical DDR for normal Linux RAM, which is not the old FPGA ring-writer architecture.
Do not print historical private IP/boot/runtime ownership values in the plate. Port/protocol details are descriptive, not deployment instructions.
review_callouts: One request per connection; a bounded number of requests is served serially.
The service invokes the frozen host02 timed controller and selects sparse mode1.
Board wall/thread timers exclude TCP input receipt and reply send. Laptop end-to-end timing has a different boundary.

notes.title: Timing boundaries differ
notes.body: Board wall / thread timers enclose the frozen controller only. TCP input receipt and reply transmission are outside those timers.

notes.title: Bounded, serialized service
notes.body: One request per connection; bounded requests served serially. Failed requests end the service without automatic retry or MMIO recovery.

notes.title: Ordinary CPU transport
notes.body: No FPGA DMA, reserved DDR ring or UDP path is active. Reference gold is not uploaded to the FPGA. This view is descriptive, not deployment guidance.

plates.title: Control, backpressure and fault containment
plates.subtitle: Waveform ready/valid and source admission credit protect state across host stalls.
review_notes: START only in IDLE, with no faults or preloaded PCM. CLEAR=1 is explicit; epoch increments on START and survives CLEAR.
All bus requests require exactly one of read/write, byteenable15, burstcount1 and aligned address; invalid registers, busy config writes and malformed PCM latch bus fault.
Hardware watchdog defaults to3,000,000,000 fabric cycles (60s at50MHz). Elapsed fabric cycles include host-induced stalls and are not isolated FFT timing.
Exporter has four storage slots but active-source credit intentionally bounds the triggered-not-emitted frame count to one. Do not show four concurrently admitted frames in this profile.
review_callouts: Taps remain valid-only. Export pressure throttles future source hops, not the tap interface itself.
The adapter responds with an error to illegal empty/full accesses; it does not wait indefinitely for data or space.
THR2 is fixed for the entire active TSH2 epoch, even though the shared core has per-frame configuration ownership.

notes.title: Admission credit is not tap ready/valid
notes.body: Export pressure limits future source hops. Four exporter slots do not mean four concurrently admitted frames in the active profile.

notes.title: Illegal accesses fail explicitly
notes.body: Full/empty illegal MMIO accesses return an error and latch a fault. Hardware watchdog: 3,000,000,000 cycles; elapsed cycles include host stalls.

plates.title: Clock, reset and verification boundaries
plates.subtitle: Active clock/reset structure and distinct evidence scopes. Dotted evidence links are not hardware signals.
review_notes: The retained board top uses HPS reset only; KEY does not cancel a pending bus response. A copied TSH1 comment does not change its instantiated TSH2 adapter.
No formal CDC/RDC, metastability proof, exhaustive code-coverage closure, PVT qualification or industrial certification is claimed.

Public portable tests cover the unchanged stream/core/exporter closure at Ns1024 and use synthetic fixtures. The broader accepted campaign includes two full384000 simulations and58physical epochs, but these are distinct evidence scopes.

The original functional RTL campaigns omit SYNTHESIS and use procedural assertions/checkers. A later supplement executes genuine UVM 1.2 and scoped local formal safety/equivalence and bounded-cover jobs on unchanged TSH2 RTL. These are separate evidence scopes; they do not establish full pipeline formal equivalence or concurrent-SVA coverage. Source-bound fit/timing is historical; creating these diagrams performs no new synthesis, simulation or hardware run.

The public repository omits generated vendor IP and full fitted build artifacts. Board wrapper clock/reset details were checked against retained sources whose hashes match the published fitted source manifest.

The reviewed S14 verification index links the UVM/formal supplement and discloses its preserved simulator startup failure and bounded recovery. The 12 completed UVM epochs include three reset recoveries, with three aborted prefixes recorded separately; local formal proofs retain explicit assumptions and exclusions.
review_callouts: No active codec RX/TX asynchronous FIFOs in this profile. Do not copy the old audio-clock diagram.
Payload RAM is generally not asynchronously reset: ownership is cleared; transform RAM is reloaded; WOLA OLA storage is explicitly scrubbed.
Representative VCD clock is10ns in simulation; physical fabric constraint is20ns. A VCD is not a board latency measurement.
